lines.text: Participant themes
Hearing the news
Participants had both fears about, and interest in, self-
needling. Some participants were apprehensive, for
example:
… am I getting the right area? (P2SSA). Nervous …
wouldn’t know what you were doing (P3NSA).
Others were very keen to do self-needling:
Very interested … I’ll do anything that might be posi-
tive (P1SSA).
Participants reported that once the therapist started
to teach them their apprehensions eased:
She explained it was just below the knee so…I thought
I can do that (P2NSA).
One participant found the experience of being
taught empowering:
…helped with my confidence to actually… learn
myself (P3NSA).
New techniques
Certain teaching techniques were new, with one prac-
titioner suggesting that the patient’s daughter might
video the self-needling:
…when I got home…it was like, “oh god I don’t want
to put it in the wrong place” …so that I could say
“come on run your video… make sure I am doing it
right” (P3SSA). …Oh that’s a good idea…it would
have been for me (P4NSA).
Some practitioners suggested that patients try doing
it on them first:
…that terrified me, I said … “I don’t want to do it on
you…no thank you [laughter] you’ll be suing me for
damage”. But you know I was amazed how easy it
goes in (P1SSA). I don’t think so no [needle the ther-
apist]…I would rather have done it to myself
(P1NSA).
One participant reported that she was shown the
technique too quickly:
…of course I’d sat there and watched … but you don’t
take it in (P2SSA). Another reported being shown
twice: I was amazed…It worked out well the more I
did it then obviously I got used to doing it. I just think
it was…just a little tap (P3NSA).
The self-needling information sheet given to all par-
ticipants was reported as being useful:
…sat there for 10 minutes and thought “I’m gonna
do this now” …I had my little booklet so I could
follow it (P1NSA).
Suggestions made by the participants included:
…people could have a measure that would show them
the distance from the landmark to the point (P3SSA).
Another participant commented: [practitioner’s]
finger measurement versus mine was quite different…
I would have been pleased if permanent marker pen
on the spots used (P2SSA).
One participant discussed ideas for locating the
points:
…tracing paper…you know …template …I’d have a
tattoo (P1NSA). I had a pen mark (P4NSA).
Another participant talked about how she stuck to
the same routine and time each week for self-
needling, including:
…do my room like a spa… you know …with whale
music…flowers [group laughter] (P5NSA).
All participants were supplied with small sharps
containers. In the southern site, two participants com-
mented about disposal. Both had tried taking the con-
tainer to a pharmacy. One participant reported:
…it was accepted (P3SSA), while another said:
( pharmacist): “Oh no we can’t have them ” …I
thought, “Oh my god what do I do with them ” …
went to a beauty salon…I just put them in the sanitary
thing (P2SSA).
Doing it again or not?
Most participants indicated in the groups that they
would self-needle again:
Yes definitely ….everything was fine (P1NSA).
Two participants reported that they would not self-
needle again. In one case this was owing to memory
problems:
